clue.text: Current classmates

definitions.meaning: a flow of water running along a channel, as in a brook
British schools group pupils of similar ability into sets, each such set of pupils sharing one level

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a STREAM is a group of pupils taught together by ability, hence 'classmates'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook's flow is a current of water, and a school's ability band is a cohort taught together as one class.

clue.text: Sent in wrong key, being dense

indicators.note: written wrong, the letters of these words are set out in a new order

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone mistyped the key in a message, being a bit slow-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SENT IN to INTENS; the musical key E finishes the word. 'dense' here means concentrated or thick, as of fog, not stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick fog can be called dense or intense, both meaning extreme in degree or concentration.

clue.text: Capital investment? This is the man to speak to

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
to address someone is to speak to them

explanation.surface: A banker's pitch about investing in the capital, with a pointer to the right contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the head and 'investment' is clothing (to invest is to clothe, as a robe invests a bishop), so a hat is a capital investment. 'This is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn on the top of one's body is literally clothing for the topmost part, a hat or crown.

clue.text: Consumer making a charge and turning colour

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: turning signals that the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A shopper makes a payment and blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer' suggests a shopper, but it is something that eats; 'turning' gives DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that feeds, an eater, is one who consumes food.

clue.text: Most reliable — rues failure in a small way

indicators.note: failure suggests the letters of rues breaking down into another order

parts.note: St is the short form of street, a way

explanation.surface: The safest option, someone regrets the collapse in a minor sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failure' rearranges RUES to SURE; ST, the abbreviation for street, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something most certain is one that can be trusted the most, the superlative of a dependable thing.

clue.text: A child among children, though mature

indicators.note: among puts one set of pieces inside the word for children

parts.note: seed in the biblical sense means offspring or children
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster in a group of kids who nonetheless seems grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children' as SEED is the biblical sense, offspring, as in 'the seed of Abraham'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned timber or a seasoned traveller is aged and experienced, i.e. fully developed.

clue.text: A country's soldiery, almost all married

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of British soldiers

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word all is dropped

explanation.surface: A nation's armed forces are nearly all wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL. RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or domain is a land under one rule, a nation.

clue.text: Well, the queen would show such a dog

parts.note: a spring is a well, a source of water
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch would surely display a fine gun dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is a noun, a water source, not an interjection. ER is the old royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer spaniel is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Offered and served without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for served goes round the hesitation

parts.note: tended means looked after or served
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A waiter offers and serves without a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but in its old sense it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something, such as a resignation or payment, is to put it forward formally.

clue.text: A vehicle crashing into a horse is dreadful

indicators.note: crashing into puts the vehicle inside the horse word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A taxi colliding with a horse is a terrible accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing into' suggests an anagram or an accident, but it is a plain insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome, involving death in a horrifying way.

clue.text: Correct a leading journalist taking people in

indicators.note: taking with in, later in the clue, means the editor takes the people inside
in completes the phrase taking in, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief journalist on a paper
men are people

explanation.surface: An editor amends a piece, bringing staff on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' reads as an adjective but is a verb, as in correcting a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to fix its errors.

clue.text: Women tend to organise such provision

indicators.note: to organise means these letters are set out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Women tend to arrange this kind of funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to organise' rearranges WOMEN TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is money given to provide a permanent income for an institution.

clue.text: A trap anyone can see through!

definitions.text: A trap anyone can see through!

parts.words: A trap anyone can see through!
parts.note: suggests an obvious ruse, but a mesh trap of knotted cord is literally see-through

explanation.definitionFit: A mesh for catching fish or birds is a trap made of holes.

clue.text: Cry for mercy before following the mean guy

indicators.note: following puts the word for before after the miser

parts.note: a miser is a mean person
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A plea for pity, ahead of tailing a stingy man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Miserere is Psalm 51, sung as a plea for mercy; it opens 'Miserere mei, Deus'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miserere, from Latin 'have mercy', is a psalm of penitence asking God's pity.

clue.text: A holiday in a cottage by the sea's terrific!

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow, across sea's and terrific

parts.words: a cottage by the sea's terrific

explanation.surface: A break in a seaside cottage is wonderful!
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run hidden across 'sea's terrific'.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the spring Christian festival, with public holidays in many countries.

clue.text: A number use a man badly to a disgusting degree

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: badly means these letters come out in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Treating a man badly endlessly is sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: D, Roman 500, is the 'number'; 'badly' rearranges USE A MAN to NAUSEAM. 'A number' looks like AN, but that leaves too few letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'to the point of sickness', said of something repeated until it nauseates.

clue.text: Learned the French assume it has value

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the French article takes in the word it

parts.note: le is the French for the
rate means value, as in rating something

explanation.surface: The French suppose something is worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' means take on, as one assumes a role, so the article holds the pronoun; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means educated, well read.

clue.text: The person of intelligence?

parts.note: suggests a clever thinker, but intelligence also means secret information gathered by agents

explanation.definitionFit: An agent works in espionage, which is called intelligence work.

clue.text: Long-suffering head accepting nice break

definitions.note: read as a noun, long-suffering is patient endurance of trouble

indicators.note: accepting means the word for head takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: break means the letters of nice are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss takes a pleasant holiday, being very tolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss and 'break' like a holiday; 'accepting' and 'break' are the working words.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the quality of enduring trouble calmly, so a noun sense of forbearance fits the long-suffering.

clue.text: A divine tot

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine or theologian

explanation.surface: A holy little child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' is the verb, as in 'tot up', not a toddler; a 'divine' is a clergyman, so DD.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up a column of figures is to sum it.

clue.text: A flowering plant so many in the end sent back

annotationWithheld.why: A flowering plant so many in the end sent back (6): read backwards MIMOSA is ASOMIM; A and SO fit, but no reading of 'many in the end' gives MIM or M + IM, and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: A flowering plant so many in the end sent back

clue.text: Note some have chosen to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat means the extracted letters go back the other way
some signals that only part of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: Notice that some people have decided to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes HOS from 'cHOSen'; 'to retreat' turns it round. SOH is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa soh is the fifth note of the scale.

clue.text: The best time to get down possibly

parts.note: a plum job is the best one, the choicest
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The best time to feel blue, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is soft feathers, not low spirits; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine fluffy feathers are one kind of a bird's feathering.

clue.text: Main loss made by Turks

indicators.note: made means these letters are worked into something new, as raw material is made into a product

explanation.surface: A heavy defeat was inflicted by the Turks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges MAIN LOSS. Osmanlis are Ottoman Turks, named after Osman I.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmanli is an old name for an Ottoman, a subject of the Turkish empire founded by Osman.

clue.text: A bit of a yarn on the beach

definitions.meaning: a single thread or fibre twisted into a rope or yarn
an old word for a shore

explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a story, but here it is thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A single thread of rope is one length, and an archaic word for shore survives in London's Strand.

clue.text: Told to go with the railway guard

parts.note: someone sent away has been told to go
Ry is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Ordered to leave with the train's guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guard' looks like the railway employee, but it defines the watchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Set up diverting warning for road-users

parts.note: to rear is to raise or set up
light means entertaining or diverting, as in light reading

explanation.surface: A diversion sign put up to alert drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverting' suggests a road diversion, but it means amusing, giving LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A red lamp on the back of a vehicle warns traffic behind it.

clue.text: Sort out the authority!

definitions.meaning: to fix or put straight a wrong
an entitlement or power to do something

explanation.definitionFit: To correct a wrong is to put it straight, and a legal entitlement gives authority to act.

clue.text: He's taken offence about a returned order

definitions.note: the definition names a man, so a man's first name fits

indicators.note: about means the word for offence goes around the other piece

parts.note: a sin is an offence

indicators.note: returned signals the order abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A man has been offended about a sent-back order.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour; 'returned' gives MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon is a common male first name, so it can stand for a 'he'.

clue.text: Staying behind, so wrapping up well

definitions.meaning: insulating material wrapped around pipes or tanks

explanation.walkthrough: LAGGING is also the British word for insulation wrapped around pipes and hot-water tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing others means falling back, and pipe insulation is the covering that keeps heat in.

clue.text: Risk putting a stop to acrimony

parts.note: an end is a stop
anger is bitterness or acrimony

explanation.surface: Gamble on ending bitter feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... to' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at hazard.

clue.text: Read an article and get hot under the collar

parts.note: to see is to read or understand
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone reads a newspaper piece and becomes furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is the grammatical word, not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be angry while silent, fuming.
